inputs.name: Chebotarev, including reduced prime progressions
inputs.statement: A prescribed conjugacy class in a finite Galois extension is represented by infinitely many unramified primes, with finite exclusions permitted.
inputs.matching: UX1 proves compatibility of the independent quadratic ramification/splitting choices; UX3 uses actual completely split auxiliary primes for the finite residual modules.

inputs.name: Finite global and local abelian reciprocity
inputs.statement: Finite unramified abelian extensions are controlled by the ideal class group; locally, abelianized inertia is the profinite unit group and its pro-ell quotient has the stated unit rank and cyclic ell-primary torsion.

primary_sources.author: J. S. Milne
primary_sources.title: Class Field Theory, version 4.03
primary_sources.location: Local reciprocity, Chapter I; global reciprocity and existence, Chapter V, Theorems 3.6--3.7 and Example 3.9

inputs.matching: Only the finite class-character and actual local unit statements are used. The cohomological and Ferrero--Washington estimates are separately supplied by prior reconstructed claims.

inputs.name: Noetherian completion and formal algebra
inputs.statement: Completion of a Noetherian local ring is faithfully flat; finite modules complete exactly; finite-variable formal power-series rings over a complete Noetherian local coefficient ring are complete Noetherian.
inputs.matching: UX6 applies this to A localized at the actual finite-residue point, and proves the universal and polynomial-line comparisons separately.

inputs.name: Krull height, finite-type dimension and completion dimensions
inputs.statement: An ideal generated by h elements has height at most h; finite-type local dimension is bounded by base dimension plus transcendence degree; completion preserves the dimension of a Noetherian local ring and of its quotient.

primary_sources.author: The Stacks Project
primary_sources.title: Dimension
primary_sources.location: Krull height theorem and systems of parameters

inputs.matching: The actual parameter counts d+20C, 2+4s and 2d-d_v+1 are proved in UX8--UX9; these dimension theorems only convert those explicit counts.

inputs.name: Grothendieck connectedness for a complete local quotient
inputs.statement: For complete Noetherian A, Y=V(I), and closed Z in Y, Y minus Z is connected when dim Z < min(c,d-1)-cd(A,I), where c is the connectedness dimension of Spec A and d its least component dimension.
inputs.matching: UX10 applies this to the regular power-series domain Lambda[[z_1,...,z_a]], whose dimension is a+1, with b defining equations, then constructs the component graph and avoids every explicit bad locus.

inputs.name: Normalization of a one-dimensional complete domain and Cohen structure
inputs.statement: A one-dimensional complete Noetherian domain has finite normalization, a complete DVR with finite residue extension; in equal characteristic a complete DVR with finite residue field is a one-variable power-series ring over that residue field.
inputs.matching: UX10 first constructs the actual one-dimensional characteristic-ell prime avoiding all bad ideals. Its normalization gives a finite residue field extension, and finite-field Teichmuller lifts preserve the original Lambda-algebra map.
